chapter: First bands, illness and Houston life
title: His mother's prayer and a Baptist upbringing
summary: His mother tells of praying for his recovery, and Cobb says he was raised strictly Baptist.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: I'm 59 until August the 10th and I'll be 60. Now Stanley, are you getting your mathematics together? I was born in 1918; August 10th.
No, but when you said you were 59 today I thought you were ...
What I was thinking now was, of course, with your family, your mother must have been very worried about you because of your problem. Age.

You know what she said to me after I came out of this thing? She said, 'Baby, the only thing I could do was pray, and I was so worried when they had given you up for dead and said it was just a matter of time.' And she said, 'I was over the sink one day, and I was washing the dishes where I'm working, and the only thing I could say, was I just prayed, and said, 'God, whatever your will is, let it be' --' and she said everything lifted off her shoulders after she said that.
Your mother was ... what religion was she?
She was Baptist, just like me.
So you were brought up as a Baptist?
Were you sort of then very strictly brought up with that religion?
Yeah. Now you take it strictly on a must, and take the two things that you can separate it, something was wrong.
